Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates enlargement of the central pulmonary arteries, specifically a prominent right descending pulmonary artery (diameter >16 mm), which is a classic radiographic sign of pulmonary hypertension associated with chronic thromboembolic disease. The cardiac silhouette appears relatively normal in size, making severe right heart failure or massive cardiomegaly less likely than mild-to-moderate pulmonary hypertension.
